chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Ali ibn Asbat from his uncle Ya'qub al-Ahmar from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to seek his advice regarding marriage. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Yes, marry, and let it be with women of religion, may your hand be dusted [with success].' He also said, 'The example of the virtuous woman is like the white crow, which is rarely found.' He asked, 'And what is the white crow?' He said, 'The one that has one white leg.'

key_terms.الْأَبْيَضُ إِحْدَى رِجْلَيْهِ: The one with one white leg (clarification of the metaphor)
key_terms.تَرِبَتْ يَدَاكَ: May your hand be dusted (an idiom for success/blessing)

ai.seo_question: What is the Prophet's advice for choosing a spouse and what does the metaphor of the white crow mean?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elaborates on the Prophet’s advice to marry women of piety by employing the metaphor of the 'white crow' (al-ghurab al-a'sam) to signify the rarity of virtuous women, clarifying that it refers to a white crow with one white leg. This imagery underscores the exceptional nature of a righteous spouse, aligning with Shia scholarly emphasis on spiritual compatibility over mere lineage or wealth. The narration serves as a practical guide for selecting a partner whose character reflects divine attributes, reinforcing the theological weight of marriage in Islamic jurisprudence.
